newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia stocks open lower, track Dow.
newsitem.headline: Australia stocks open lower, track Dow.

text.p: The Australian share market opened lower on Tuesday, with the tone set by the weaker Dow close and lingering concern about profit downgrades by major companies.
At 10.25 a.m. (2325 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was 12.1 points lower at 2371.7.
The December share price index was 9.0 points weaker at 2,389.0, regaining some ground from an even lower opening and giving brokers some hope that the decline was half-hearted.
"I think the market will head lower all day, most pressure will be on the big companies," said the head of the institutional dealing desk at one European brokerage firm.
The overnight rise in the copper price to a five-month high was offset by a disappointing fall in nickel, effectively cancelling any short-term gains for resource stocks.

Nickel fell to a two-year low on the LME, with the local effect evident in early trade as shares in key producer WMC fell 13 cents to A$7.65 (US$6.07). Copper majors BHP and CRA also eased, with BHP down 11 at A$17.73 and CRA 14 lower at A$19.46.

"Nickel was belted last night, that's the reason for resource stocks losing their confidence," said another institutional dealer. Anaconda Nickel, the owner of the Murrin Murrin project, was 26 cents lower at A$4.20.
The nation's largest bottler, Coca-Cola Amatil, was dumped by investors for a second day after revealing last Friday that its earlier 1996/97 profit forecasts had been withdrawn.
CC-Amatil was 17 cents lower at A$15.35, with one broker saying the stock should recover most of its early losses.

Building products group Boral was three cents lower at A$3.14 after telling investors on Monday that its early fiscal year result was worse than year ago. Among other key industrial stocks, transporter Brambles was 20 cents lower at A$21.90.
Brokers said the mild turnover levels in early trade indicated the overall market was not set for a prolonged fall.
